mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the inflation signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over the past 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the labor market signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) over the past 6 months signals strengthening demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past 3 months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the supply contraction signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the past month signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the labor market signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Housing Starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% and Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) increase by more than 2% over the past 3 months, it signals a robust demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% and RSAFS increase > 2% in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the demand signal, or the joint correlation between HOUST and RSAFS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% annualized over the past 3 months, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the monetary tightening signal, or the joint correlation between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL conditions and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a recessionary regime, a decrease in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the past 6 months signals a severe contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to heightened economic slowdown concerns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances during a recession despite the supply contraction signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during recessions.
